name: Gorgias
subcategory: help desks, live chat and support knowledge
tagline: Build a small ecommerce support inbox from email and store webhooks

pricing.notes: Official Basic monthly package; ticket volume affects higher tiers.

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.limits: 50 billable tickets/month; 3 user seats; email only; 2 API requests/second
tiers.notes: Monthly only; annual billing is unavailable on Starter.

tiers.name: Basic
tiers.limits: 300 billable tickets/month; up to 500 user seats; 2 API requests/second; unlimited stores
tiers.notes: A ticket is billable when a human, Rule or AI Agent replies; a renewed thread can become a new ticket after inactivity.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 2,000 billable tickets/month; up to 500 user seats; 2 API requests/second; unlimited stores

tiers.name: Advanced
tiers.limits: 5,000 billable tickets/month; up to 500 user seats; 2 API requests/second; unlimited stores

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: More than 5,000 billable tickets/month; up to 500 user seats; 4 API requests/second

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier (7-day trial; no card; all features available during trial)
pricing.billingTerms: Starter monthly only; Basic, Pro, Advanced and Enterprise monthly + annual (annual billed upfront; about 16% off / 2 months free)
pricing.hiddenCosts: Ticket overages are $0.40 each on Starter/Basic, $0.36 each on Pro/Advanced, and custom on Enterprise. AI Agent costs $1.00 per resolved interaction monthly or $0.90 annually, and each AI interaction also consumes a helpdesk ticket; AI overage is $1.50. Voice and SMS are paid add-ons, and applicable sales tax is extra.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Gorgias, build a small ecommerce support inbox from email and store webhooks. The hard boundary is deep commerce integrations, order actions, automation, ai, and high-volume support operations, plus channel integrations and support operations.
coreLoopDIY: Receive customer messages from email and store webhooks into a small shared ecommerce support inbox, reply from one place, and retain a searchable conversation history.
whatYouLose: deep commerce integrations, order actions, automation, AI, and high-volume support operations
ongoingBurden: message delivery, webhooks, threading, identity, permissions, attachments, notifications, spam, search, uptime, and retention
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Gorgias because support software survives because missing or misrouting one customer message is expensive and every channel behaves differently. The recurring cost buys message delivery, webhooks, threading, identity, permissions, attachments, notifications, spam, search, uptime, and retention, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Chatwoot
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source customer engagement and shared-inbox platform.

alternatives.name: Chatwoot
alternatives.desc: Email and Shopify conversations share one inbox; useful ecommerce plumbing, minus Gorgias's deeper store automations.

alternatives.name: tawk.to
alternatives.desc: A free shared inbox with a Shopify order tab; the AI order bot is where the bill starts.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Basic plan and a small-team shared inbox DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Gorgias in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, WebSockets, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: receive customer messages from email and store webhooks into a small shared ecommerce support inbox, reply from one place, and retain a searchable conversation history.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement one workspace, agents, contacts, inboxes, conversations, messages, labels, and assignment.
Provide a website chat widget with reconnect, unread counts, file limits, and clear availability state.
Create a shared inbox with filters, collision warnings, notes, canned replies, and searchable history.
Add email notifications, browser notifications, and an immutable assignment and status log.
Implement spam controls, attachment scanning hooks, retention settings, export, and contact deletion.
Ship Docker Compose, backups, health checks, migrations, and a documented admin recovery flow.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out many social and messaging channels.
Deliberately leave out AI agents trained on proprietary support data.
Deliberately leave out enterprise workforce management, SSO, and compliance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
